note: Agricultural Science round 1 (part A): general agriculture (meaning/importance, ecology, genetics, inputs/history/agencies) and agronomy (soils, soil water and conservation, fertility, tillage, plant form and growth, propagation, cropping systems, crop husbandry, pasture and floriculture, weeds, diseases, pests, forestry) - with a genetics cross, a fertiliser calculation, a cassava variety trial and a planting case as passages.

passages.title: Crossing tall and dwarf maize
passages.text: In maize, tallness (T) is dominant over dwarfness (t). A farmer crossed a pure-breeding tall plant with a pure-breeding dwarf plant. All the F1 plants were tall. He then self-pollinated the F1 plants and harvested 400 F2 seedlings.

passages.title: Fertiliser for Musa's maize farm
passages.text: Musa wants to apply nitrogen at 60 kg N per hectare to his 2.5-hectare maize farm. He can buy either urea (46% N) at ₦30,000 per 50 kg bag or NPK 15-15-15 at ₦25,000 per 50 kg bag.

passages.title: Cassava trial plots
passages.text:
Four cassava varieties were planted on
plots of equal size (0.25 ha each) at the
same spacing and harvested after 12
months.

Variety   Yield (t)   Mosaic score
TMS-1        7.5          1
TMS-2        5.0          2
Local-A      3.0          4
Local-B      3.5          3

Mosaic score: 1 = no symptoms, 5 = severe
symptoms.

passages.title: Planting Ngozi's maize
passages.text: Ngozi planted maize on one hectare at a spacing of 75 cm between rows and 25 cm within rows, one seed per hole. Germination was 80%. She later intercropped the maize with cowpea and applied poultry manure before planting.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The genotype of the F1 plants is
questions.B: Tt and tt in equal numbers
questions.explanation: Each parent contributes one allele: T from the tall parent and t from the dwarf parent, giving heterozygous Tt.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The expected number of dwarf plants among the 400 F2 seedlings is
questions.explanation: Selfing Tt × Tt gives 3 tall : 1 dwarf; ¼ × 400 = 100 dwarf plants.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The expected number of F2 plants that are homozygous tall is
questions.explanation: The F2 genotypic ratio is 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so ¼ × 400 = 100 are TT.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The observation that all F1 plants were tall illustrates Mendel's
questions.explanation: In a cross between contrasting pure lines, only the dominant character appears in the F1 generation.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: If an F1 plant is test-crossed with a dwarf plant, the expected phenotypic ratio of the offspring is
questions.explanation: Tt × tt gives ½ Tt (tall) and ½ tt (dwarf); a test cross reveals the heterozygous genotype.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The percentage of the F2 tall plants that would breed true when selfed is approximately
questions.explanation: Of the tall F2 plants, 1 TT : 2 Tt; only the TT third breed true, about 33%.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The total quantity of nitrogen Musa needs for his farm is
questions.explanation: 60 kg N/ha × 2.5 ha = 150 kg N.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The quantity of urea required to supply 150 kg of nitrogen is approximately
questions.explanation: Urea is 46% N, so 150 ÷ 0.46 ≈ 326 kg of urea.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The quantity of NPK 15-15-15 required to supply the same 150 kg of nitrogen is

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The cost of supplying the nitrogen with urea (to the nearest whole bag) is
questions.explanation: 326 kg ÷ 50 kg = 6.5 → 7 bags × ₦30,000 = ₦210,000, compared with 20 bags of NPK costing ₦500,000.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Apart from cost, an advantage of NPK 15-15-15 over urea on Musa's farm is that it
questions.C: does not need to be applied
questions.explanation: A compound fertiliser supplies three major nutrients at once; urea is a straight nitrogen fertiliser.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The best method of applying the urea to the growing maize is
questions.A: broadcasting on the leaves at noon
questions.B: burning it with the crop residue
questions.C: dissolving it in the irrigation reservoir once a year
questions.D: side dressing (band placement) a few centimetres from the plants, then covering
questions.explanation: Side dressing at about 3–4 weeks after planting places the nitrogen near the roots and reduces loss by volatilisation.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The yield of TMS-1 per hectare is
questions.explanation: 7.5 t on 0.25 ha = 7.5 × 4 = 30 t per hectare.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The variety most susceptible to cassava mosaic disease is
questions.explanation: Local-A scored 4, the highest disease score in the trial, and gave the lowest yield.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The trial suggests that yield is
questions.C: higher in varieties with higher mosaic scores
questions.D: higher in varieties with lower mosaic scores
questions.explanation: TMS-1 (score 1) yielded most and Local-A (score 4) least; disease resistance improves yield.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The average yield of the two local varieties per hectare is
questions.explanation: (3.0 + 3.5) ÷ 2 = 3.25 t per plot = 13 t per hectare.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following was a controlled variable in the trial?
questions.explanation: Plot size, spacing and harvest date were kept the same so that only variety differed.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: TMS varieties were developed by the
questions.C: Nigerian Institute for Oil Palm Research
questions.D: International Institute of Tropical Agriculture, Ibadan
questions.explanation: Tropical Manioc Selection (TMS) lines resistant to mosaic disease were bred at IITA, Ibadan.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The plant population per hectare at Ngozi's spacing (before germination loss) is

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The number of maize plants that actually established is about

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Growing maize and cowpea together on the same field at the same time is called
questions.explanation: Intercropping (mixed cropping) spreads risk and uses land, light and labour more fully.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: One benefit of the cowpea to the maize in this system is that cowpea
questions.B: attracts stem borers away from itself
questions.C: fixes atmospheric nitrogen through root nodules
questions.explanation: Legumes host Rhizobium bacteria that convert atmospheric nitrogen into forms plants can use.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Poultry manure is classified as
questions.explanation: Animal droppings, compost and green manure are organic manures that improve soil structure as well as supplying nutrients.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Ngozi could have improved the germination percentage by
questions.A: planting the seeds deeper than 10 cm in the ridge
questions.B: planting the seed in the middle of the dry season
questions.C: using viable treated seed planted at the right depth in moist soil
questions.D: increasing the spacing between the rows to 1 m
questions.explanation: Seed viability, seed dressing against soil pests, planting depth of 3–5 cm and adequate soil moisture determine germination.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Meaning, Scope and Importance of Agriculture
questions.q: Agriculture is best defined as the
questions.A: growing of crops on large farms for sale
questions.B: study of soils and the rocks from which they form
questions.C: rearing of cattle, sheep and goats by nomads
questions.D: production of crops and animals, with their processing and marketing
questions.explanation: Modern agriculture covers production, processing, storage, distribution and marketing of plant and animal products.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Meaning, Scope and Importance of Agriculture
questions.q: The branch of agriculture concerned with the cultivation of fruits, vegetables and ornamental plants is
questions.explanation: Horticulture includes pomology (fruits), olericulture (vegetables) and floriculture (flowers).

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Meaning, Scope and Importance of Agriculture
questions.q: The study of field crops and soil management is known as
questions.explanation: Agronomy deals with crops such as maize, rice and cassava and the soils that support them.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Meaning, Scope and Importance of Agriculture
questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of subsistence agriculture?
questions.A: use of large farm machinery on extensive land
questions.B: production of one crop for export to other countries
questions.C: production mainly for family consumption on small holdings
questions.D: employment of many hired workers throughout the year
questions.explanation: Subsistence farmers use simple tools, family labour and small plots; surpluses, if any, are sold locally.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Meaning, Scope and Importance of Agriculture
questions.q: A disadvantage of commercial agriculture is that it
questions.A: produces little surplus for sale in the market
questions.B: cannot produce enough food to feed the towns
questions.C: uses only family labour and simple hand tools
questions.D: requires large capital and can degrade the environment
questions.explanation: Large-scale farming needs heavy investment in land, machinery and inputs, and monoculture invites pests and soil exhaustion.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Meaning, Scope and Importance of Agriculture
questions.q: Which agro-allied industry uses cotton lint as its raw material?
questions.explanation: Textile mills spin and weave cotton; tanneries use hides and skins; breweries use sorghum and barley.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Meaning, Scope and Importance of Agriculture
questions.q: Which of the following is a contribution of agriculture to the economy of West Africa?
questions.A: increase in unemployment in the rural areas
questions.B: destruction of forests and wildlife habitats
questions.C: reduction of development in the rural areas
questions.D: provision of food, employment, raw materials and foreign exchange
questions.explanation: Agriculture employs most of the workforce and supplies food and raw materials for industry and export.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Meaning, Scope and Importance of Agriculture
questions.q: Sericulture is the rearing of
questions.explanation: Silkworms produce silk; apiculture is bee-keeping and heliculture is snail farming.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Meaning, Scope and Importance of Agriculture
questions.q: The rearing of fish in ponds is called
questions.explanation: Pisciculture (fish farming) is a branch of aquaculture.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Meaning, Scope and Importance of Agriculture
questions.q: One problem of subsistence agriculture in West Africa is
questions.A: over-production of food crops for the market
questions.B: excess mechanisation of the small family farms
questions.C: too much capital invested in small farms
questions.D: low output due to small holdings and crude implements
questions.explanation: Fragmented holdings, hoes and cutlasses, and low inputs keep yields and incomes low.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Meaning, Scope and Importance of Agriculture
questions.q: The agro-allied industry that depends on oil palm products is
questions.explanation: Palm oil and palm kernel oil are raw materials for soap, margarine and cosmetics.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Meaning, Scope and Importance of Agriculture
questions.q: A farmer who grows cocoa mainly for sale but keeps a small plot of yam and vegetables for the family is practising
questions.A: pure subsistence agriculture with no crop for sale
questions.B: nomadic farming that moves from place to place
questions.C: commercial agriculture with a subsistence component
questions.D: plantation agriculture on a large estate
questions.explanation: Most West African farmers combine a cash crop with food crops for the household.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The ecological zone of West Africa with the highest rainfall and dense evergreen trees is the
questions.explanation: The forest zone receives over 1,500 mm of rain and supports cocoa, oil palm, rubber and kola.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Groundnut, cotton and millet are typical crops of the
questions.explanation: The Sudan savanna has a short rainy season, sandy soils and abundant sunshine suited to these crops.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a biotic factor affecting crop production?
questions.explanation: Biotic factors are living organisms (pests, diseases, weeds, predators, pollinators); the others are abiotic.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The main factor that determines the distribution of crops across the ecological zones of West Africa is
questions.A: the colour and depth of the soil in each zone
questions.B: the altitude of the land above sea level alone
questions.C: the direction of the prevailing wind in each zone
questions.D: the amount and distribution of rainfall in each zone
questions.explanation: Rainfall decreases from the coast northwards, changing vegetation from forest to Sahel and the crops that can be grown.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Cattle rearing is concentrated in the savanna zones mainly because
questions.A: of the abundance of tall trees for shade
questions.B: there is more rainfall than in the forest
questions.C: the zones have grassland and few tsetse flies
questions.D: there are no crop farmers in the zones
questions.explanation: Tsetse flies, which transmit trypanosomiasis, thrive in the humid forest zone.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Relative humidity affects crop production because high humidity
questions.A: prevents all plant growth in the forest zone
questions.B: removes plant nutrients from the soil
questions.C: kills all the insects that attack crops
questions.D: encourages fungal diseases and slows the drying of produce
questions.explanation: Humid conditions favour fungi such as black pod of cocoa and make sun-drying of grains difficult.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The ecological zone lying between the forest and the Sudan savanna is the
questions.explanation: The Guinea savanna, with tall grasses and scattered trees, is West Africa's main producer of yam, maize and rice.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following crops is suited to the Sahel zone?
questions.explanation: Drought-tolerant cereals with short growing periods suit the Sahel's low, unreliable rainfall.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Temperature affects crop production by influencing
questions.A: the colour of the soil and its depth
questions.B: the amount of nitrogen present in the air
questions.C: the rate of germination, growth and maturity of crops
questions.D: the number of hours the farmer works
questions.explanation: Each crop has an optimum temperature range; wheat needs cooler conditions than maize.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A farmer in the rainforest zone wishing to grow cattle would face the greatest problem from
questions.A: excess grass and fodder in the forest
questions.B: cold temperatures in the forest zone
questions.C: lack of drinking water for the animals
questions.D: trypanosomiasis spread by tsetse fly and high humidity
questions.explanation: Only trypano-tolerant breeds such as the N'dama and Muturu survive well in the forest zone.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Light is important to crops because it is needed for
questions.explanation: Day length controls flowering in short-day and long-day plants, and light energy drives photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The mangrove swamp zone is characterised by
questions.A: dry sandy soils and low rainfall
questions.D: saline waterlogged soils and tidal influence
questions.explanation: Mangrove swamps along the coast support fishing and, where reclaimed, swamp rice.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The physical appearance of an organism resulting from its genes is called its
questions.explanation: Phenotype (e.g. tall) is the expression of the genotype (e.g. TT or Tt) in a given environment.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Alternative forms of a gene occupying the same position on homologous chromosomes are called
questions.explanation: T and t are alleles for height; the locus is the position of the gene on the chromosome.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The type of cell division that produces gametes with half the chromosome number is
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number so that fertilisation restores the diploid number.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: In crop and animal breeding, Mendel's first law (law of segregation) states that
questions.A: genes for different characters are inherited together in one group
questions.B: characters acquired during life are passed on to the offspring
questions.C: all the offspring of a cross resemble the male parent in every way
questions.D: the two alleles of a pair separate so that each gamete carries only one
questions.explanation: Each gamete receives one member of each allele pair.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: In a cross between two heterozygous red-flowered plants (Rr), where red is dominant, the proportion of white-flowered offspring is
questions.explanation: Rr × Rr gives RR, Rr, Rr, rr; only rr (¼) is white.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: An organism with two identical alleles for a character is described as
questions.explanation: TT and tt are homozygous; Tt is heterozygous (hybrid).

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The introduction of a new crop variety from another country into the local farming system is called
questions.explanation: Introduction is the quickest improvement method but the new variety must be tested for adaptation and screened through quarantine.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Plant quarantine is important in crop improvement because it
questions.A: increases the yield of the crop directly
questions.B: produces new hybrids from imported material
questions.C: keeps foreign pests and diseases out of imported planting material
questions.D: replaces the need for fertiliser on the farm
questions.explanation: Introduced materials are isolated and inspected before release to farmers.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The mating of closely related animals, such as sire to daughter, is called
questions.explanation: Inbreeding fixes desirable characters but may expose harmful recessive genes and reduce vigour.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The increased vigour and productivity shown by the offspring of two different breeds or varieties is called
questions.explanation: Hybrid maize and cross-bred cattle outperform their parents because of heterosis.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Artificial insemination in cattle involves
questions.A: mating a bull with many cows naturally in the paddock
questions.B: castrating young bulls to improve their meat quality
questions.C: transferring embryos from one cow to another cow
questions.D: depositing semen from a superior bull in the cow's reproductive tract
questions.explanation: AI spreads the genes of one superior bull to thousands of cows and reduces the spread of venereal diseases.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A pure-breeding black rabbit (BB) is crossed with a white rabbit (bb). The F1 rabbits are all black. If the F1 rabbits are mated among themselves, the proportion of black rabbits in the F2 that are heterozygous is
questions.explanation: F2 genotypes are 1 BB : 2 Bb : 1 bb; among the three black rabbits, two are Bb, i.e. ⅔.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a reason for crop improvement?
questions.A: to reduce the yield of the crop per hectare
questions.B: to increase the susceptibility of crops to disease
questions.C: to develop high-yielding varieties resistant to pests and drought
questions.D: to lengthen the period the crop takes to mature
questions.explanation: Breeding also aims at early maturity, uniform ripening and better nutritional quality.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: In animal breeding, the crossing of two different breeds, such as White Fulani with Friesian, is called
questions.explanation: Cross-breeding combines the hardiness of the local breed with the milk yield of the exotic breed.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The scientist regarded as the father of genetics is
questions.explanation: Mendel's experiments with garden peas (1866) established the laws of inheritance.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The stage of mitosis during which chromosomes line up at the equator of the cell is
questions.explanation: Metaphase is followed by anaphase, when the chromatids separate to opposite poles.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A dihybrid cross between two plants heterozygous for two independently assorting characters (AaBb × AaBb) gives a phenotypic ratio of
questions.explanation: Mendel's second law (independent assortment) predicts 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 in the F2 of a dihybrid cross.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a farm input?
questions.explanation: Inputs are the resources put into production: seeds, fertilisers, agrochemicals, feed, labour, machinery and water.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Agrochemicals include
questions.D: silos, cribs, rhombus stores and barns
questions.explanation: Agrochemicals are chemical inputs used to nourish crops and control pests, diseases and weeds.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The traditional farming system in which land is cultivated for a few years and then left to rest while the farmer moves to a new area is
questions.explanation: Where the settlement is permanent and only the plots rotate, the system is called bush fallowing.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Bush fallowing differs from shifting cultivation in that in bush fallowing
questions.A: the farmer moves his home to a new site each year
questions.B: only tree crops such as cocoa and kola are grown
questions.C: no fallow period is allowed between the crops
questions.D: the farmer's home is permanent while the plots are rotated
questions.explanation: Population pressure has shortened fallow periods, reducing the system's ability to restore fertility.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The land tenure system in which land belongs to the community and is allocated by the chief or family head is
questions.explanation: Communal tenure gives security to members but discourages long-term investment and use of land as loan collateral.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A major problem of agricultural development in West Africa is
questions.A: over-supply of credit to small farmers by banks
questions.B: too much research by the agricultural institutes
questions.C: excess mechanisation of the small family farms
questions.D: inadequate infrastructure such as roads, storage and irrigation
questions.explanation: Poor roads raise transport costs and cause post-harvest losses; lack of finance, land tenure and pests add to the problem.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The Cocoa Research Institute of Nigeria (CRIN) is located at
questions.explanation: CRIN, Ibadan, researches cocoa, kola, coffee, cashew and tea.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The Nigerian Institute for Oil Palm Research (NIFOR) is located near
questions.explanation: NIFOR at Benin City works on oil palm, coconut, date palm and raphia.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The Institute for Agricultural Research (IAR), which works on crops of the northern savanna, is located at
questions.explanation: IAR, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, researches sorghum, millet, cowpea, cotton and groundnut.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The National Root Crops Research Institute (NRCRI) is located at
questions.explanation: NRCRI, Umudike (Abia State), researches cassava, yam, cocoyam, sweet potato and ginger.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The National Cereals Research Institute (NCRI) is located at
questions.explanation: NCRI, Badeggi (Niger State), works on rice, soya bean, benniseed and sugar cane.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The Forestry Research Institute of Nigeria (FRIN) is located at
questions.explanation: FRIN, Ibadan, researches forestry, wildlife and agroforestry.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a role of government in agricultural development?
questions.A: banning agricultural research in the universities
questions.B: increasing the price of fertiliser to the farmers
questions.C: provision of extension services, subsidised inputs, credit and roads
questions.explanation: Governments also formulate policies, establish research institutes and guarantee minimum prices.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Non-governmental organisations (NGOs) contribute to agriculture by
questions.A: collecting taxes and levies from farmers
questions.B: owning all the farmland in the rural areas
questions.C: controlling the weather over the farming areas
questions.D: training farmers and providing micro-credit and improved technology
questions.explanation: NGOs such as Sasakawa Global 2000 and IFAD-supported programmes work directly with small farmers.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The Agricultural Development Programmes (ADPs) in Nigerian states were established mainly to
questions.A: export crops to other countries for revenue
questions.B: build universities of agriculture in each state
questions.C: give small farmers extension, inputs and rural roads
questions.D: regulate fishing in the rivers and lakes
questions.explanation: ADPs, started with World Bank support in the 1970s, use the training-and-visit extension system.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Operation Feed the Nation (OFN) was launched in Nigeria in
questions.explanation: OFN (1976) under General Obasanjo aimed at food self-sufficiency; the Green Revolution followed in 1980.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The Rubber Research Institute of Nigeria is located at
questions.explanation: RRIN at Iyanomo researches natural rubber and gum arabic.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following inputs is a planting material?
questions.explanation: Planting materials include seeds, cuttings, suckers, setts, tubers and seedlings.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Rocks, Soil Formation and Soil Types
questions.q: Rocks formed by the cooling and solidification of molten magma are called
questions.explanation: Granite and basalt are igneous; sandstone is sedimentary; marble is metamorphic.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Rocks, Soil Formation and Soil Types
questions.q: The process by which rocks are broken down into smaller particles to form soil is called
questions.explanation: Weathering may be physical (temperature changes, water, wind), chemical (hydrolysis, oxidation, carbonation) or biological.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Rocks, Soil Formation and Soil Types
questions.q: Which of the following is a factor of soil formation?
questions.A: the price of land in the area
questions.B: the income of the farmer who owns it
questions.C: the type of crop grown on the land
questions.D: parent material, climate, relief, organisms and time
questions.explanation: These five factors interact to determine the type of soil that develops in a place.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Rocks, Soil Formation and Soil Types
questions.q: Soil formed in place from the weathering of the rock beneath it is called
questions.explanation: Transported soils are moved by water (alluvial), wind (aeolian), gravity (colluvial) or ice (glacial).

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Rocks, Soil Formation and Soil Types
questions.q: The soil constituent that gives soil its dark colour and improves water-holding capacity is
questions.explanation: Humus is decomposed organic matter; it supplies nutrients and binds particles into crumbs.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Rocks, Soil Formation and Soil Types
questions.q: A soil made up of about 40% sand, 40% silt and 20% clay is described as
questions.explanation: Loam has a balanced texture, good drainage and nutrient retention, and is best for most crops.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Rocks, Soil Formation and Soil Types
questions.q: The property of soil that refers to the relative proportions of sand, silt and clay is
questions.explanation: Texture is determined by mechanical analysis or by the feel method; structure is the arrangement of particles into aggregates.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Rocks, Soil Formation and Soil Types
questions.q: Which soil type has the largest particles and drains most rapidly?
questions.explanation: Sand particles are 0.02–2 mm; water passes through quickly and nutrients are easily leached.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Rocks, Soil Formation and Soil Types
questions.q: Clay soil is described as heavy because it
questions.A: weighs more per particle than sand
questions.C: is sticky when wet and hard to cultivate when dry
questions.D: has no pores at all for water and air
questions.explanation: The tiny plate-like clay particles hold water tightly and pack closely.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Rocks, Soil Formation and Soil Types
questions.q: The layer of the soil profile richest in organic matter is the
questions.explanation: Crop roots feed mainly in the topsoil; the B horizon accumulates leached materials.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Rocks, Soil Formation and Soil Types
questions.q: A soil pH of 5.0 indicates that the soil is
questions.explanation: pH below 7 is acidic; most crops grow best between pH 6.0 and 7.0. Lime is applied to raise the pH.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Rocks, Soil Formation and Soil Types
questions.q: Which of the following components of soil is a living constituent?
questions.B: soil air held in the pore spaces
questions.D: soil water held in the pores
questions.explanation: Soil organisms decompose organic matter, fix nitrogen and improve aeration.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Rocks, Soil Formation and Soil Types
questions.q: A soil sample of 100 g was found to contain 70 g of sand, 20 g of silt and 10 g of clay. It is classified as
questions.explanation: With 70% sand and enough silt and clay to give some cohesion, the soil is a sandy loam.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Rocks, Soil Formation and Soil Types
questions.q: The chemical weathering process in which water reacts with minerals in rock is
questions.explanation: Hydrolysis converts feldspar in granite into clay minerals.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Rocks, Soil Formation and Soil Types
questions.q: Sedimentary rocks such as limestone and sandstone are formed by
questions.A: the cooling of magma inside the crust
questions.B: the eruption of lava from volcanoes
questions.C: great heat and pressure deep in the earth
questions.D: deposition and consolidation of sediments in layers
questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks weather to give soils rich in bases (limestone) or sandy soils (sandstone).

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Rocks, Soil Formation and Soil Types
questions.q: Soil structure that is most desirable for crop production is
questions.explanation: Crumb structure gives good aeration, drainage, root penetration and workability.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Water held in the soil pores against gravity and available to plants is called
questions.explanation: Capillary water is the main source of water for crops; hygroscopic water is held too tightly to be used.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The amount of water a soil holds after excess gravitational water has drained away is its
questions.explanation: Field capacity is the upper limit of available water; the permanent wilting point is the lower limit.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The soil moisture level at which plants can no longer extract water and wilt permanently is the
questions.explanation: Between field capacity and wilting point lies the available water for crops.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The removal of top soil by water or wind is called
questions.explanation: Erosion removes the fertile topsoil; leaching washes nutrients down the profile.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The type of water erosion that removes a thin uniform layer of soil from a wide area is
questions.explanation: Sheet erosion is followed by rills and, if unchecked, gullies.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The first stage of water erosion, in which raindrops detach soil particles, is
questions.explanation: Mulching and cover crops protect the soil surface from raindrop impact.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following practices controls erosion on sloping land?
questions.A: ploughing up and down the slope each season
questions.B: overgrazing of the slope by cattle and goats
questions.C: clean clearing of all vegetation before planting
questions.D: contour ploughing, terracing and strip cropping
questions.explanation: These practices slow run-off and hold soil in place.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The covering of the soil surface with dry grass, leaves or plastic to conserve moisture is called
questions.explanation: Mulch reduces evaporation, moderates soil temperature, suppresses weeds and adds organic matter.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Planting rows of trees across the direction of the prevailing wind to protect crops is called
questions.explanation: Wind breaks reduce wind erosion and evaporation in the savanna zones.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The artificial application of water to crops during dry periods is called
questions.explanation: Methods include surface (flood, furrow, basin), sprinkler (overhead) and drip (trickle) irrigation.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The method of irrigation that delivers water slowly to the base of each plant through pipes and emitters is
questions.explanation: Drip irrigation saves water and is ideal for vegetables and orchards in dry areas.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Drainage is necessary on farmland because waterlogged soils
questions.A: have too much air in their pore spaces
questions.B: lack oxygen for root respiration and soil organisms
questions.C: are always very fertile and productive
questions.D: cannot be eroded by water or wind
questions.explanation: Waterlogging suffocates roots, encourages denitrification and root diseases, and delays tillage.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of sprinkler irrigation?
questions.A: it wastes a lot of water through run-off
questions.B: it needs no equipment or pumping
questions.C: it suits uneven land and applies water uniformly
questions.D: it causes gully erosion on the farm
questions.explanation: Sprinklers work on sloping or uneven land but are costly and affected by wind.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A farmer noticed that after heavy rain the water on his sandy soil disappeared quickly but his neighbour's clay soil remained wet for days. The difference is due mainly to
questions.A: the colour of the two soils
questions.B: the presence of earthworms in the clay soil
questions.C: the higher humus content of sandy soil
questions.D: the larger pores and faster percolation in sandy soil
questions.explanation: Sandy soils have large pores and low water-holding capacity, so they drain fast; clay retains water in tiny pores.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The downward movement of water through the soil is called
questions.explanation: Percolation replenishes groundwater but also carries dissolved nutrients downward (leaching).

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a cause of soil erosion?
questions.explanation: Removing vegetation exposes bare soil to rain and wind.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The three major (macro) nutrients supplied by NPK fertiliser are
questions.explanation: N promotes leafy growth, P root and flower development, K disease resistance and fruit quality.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A crop showing yellowing of older leaves and stunted growth is most likely deficient in
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is mobile in the plant, so deficiency shows first on older leaves as chlorosis.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Purple colouration of maize leaves and poor root development indicate deficiency of
questions.explanation: Phosphorus deficiency causes purpling of leaves, poor rooting and delayed maturity.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Scorching (browning) of the leaf margins and weak stalks are symptoms of deficiency of
questions.explanation: Potassium deficiency shows as marginal leaf scorch and lodging.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a micro-nutrient (trace element)?
questions.explanation: Micro-nutrients (Fe, Mn, Zn, Cu, B, Mo, Cl) are needed in very small amounts.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A fertiliser labelled 20-10-10 contains
questions.explanation: The grade gives the percentages of N, P₂O₅ and K₂O in that order.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The quantity of nitrogen in a 50 kg bag of NPK 20-10-10 is
questions.explanation: The first figure of the grade is the percentage of nitrogen: 20% of 50 kg = 10 kg N.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a straight (single-nutrient) fertiliser?
questions.explanation: Urea (46% N), single superphosphate and muriate of potash each supply mainly one nutrient.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The process by which soluble nutrients are washed down beyond the reach of plant roots is
questions.explanation: Leaching is severe in high-rainfall sandy soils and removes nitrates and bases.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The practice of growing different crops on the same land in a planned sequence to maintain fertility is
questions.explanation: Rotation with legumes restores nitrogen, breaks pest cycles and uses nutrients from different soil depths.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Green manuring involves
questions.A: applying green paint to the surface of the soil
questions.B: spraying a green-coloured herbicide on weeds
questions.C: ploughing a young leguminous crop into the soil to decay
questions.D: harvesting crops before they are fully ripe
questions.explanation: Crops such as mucuna and cowpea are turned in at flowering to add nitrogen and organic matter.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Lime is applied to soils in order to
questions.A: increase the acidity of the soil
questions.B: lower the water table of the farm
questions.C: kill weeds growing in the soil
questions.D: reduce acidity and supply calcium to the soil
questions.explanation: Liming materials include calcium carbonate, calcium oxide and dolomite.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria found in the root nodules of legumes belong to the genus
questions.explanation: Rhizobium lives symbiotically in legume roots; Azotobacter fixes nitrogen freely in the soil.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The conversion of ammonia to nitrite and then to nitrate by soil bacteria is called
questions.explanation: Nitrosomonas produces nitrite and Nitrobacter converts it to nitrate, the form most plants absorb.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Denitrification, the loss of soil nitrogen as nitrogen gas, occurs mainly in
questions.explanation: Anaerobic bacteria reduce nitrates to nitrogen gas when oxygen is scarce.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A farmer applied 200 kg of single superphosphate (18% P₂O₅) to one hectare. The quantity of P₂O₅ applied per hectare is
questions.explanation: 18% of 200 kg = 36 kg P₂O₅.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Farmyard manure differs from inorganic fertiliser in that farmyard manure
questions.B: contains higher concentrations of N, P and K
questions.C: improves soil structure and releases nutrients slowly
questions.explanation: Organic manures are bulky and low in nutrients but improve physical properties and microbial life.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Compost is prepared by
questions.B: drying animal bones in the sun
questions.C: mixing sand and clay in equal parts
questions.D: decomposing plant and animal wastes in heaps or pits
questions.explanation: Alternate layers of plant residues, manure and soil are kept moist and turned to speed decomposition.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a method of fertiliser application?
questions.explanation: Methods include broadcasting, ring/band placement, side dressing, top dressing, drilling and foliar spraying.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Soil fertility is best defined as the
questions.A: amount of water stored in the soil
questions.B: depth of the topsoil above the subsoil
questions.C: ability of a soil to supply adequate nutrients for crop growth
questions.D: size of the particles that make up the soil
questions.explanation: Productivity also depends on physical properties, climate and management.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following practices leads to loss of soil fertility?
questions.explanation: Continuous removal of nutrients in harvested crops and destruction of organic matter by fire deplete the soil.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The first operation in preparing bush land for cultivation is
questions.explanation: Clearing (felling, cutting and removing vegetation) is followed by stumping, ploughing, harrowing and ridging.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The primary tillage operation that cuts, breaks and inverts the soil is
questions.explanation: Ploughing buries weeds and residues and opens the soil; harrowing (secondary tillage) breaks the clods.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The implement used for secondary tillage to break clods and level the seedbed is the
questions.explanation: Disc and spike-tooth harrows follow the plough to produce a fine tilth.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Ridges are made on farmland mainly to
questions.A: reduce the depth of the soil available to roots
questions.B: provide a deep loose seedbed with good drainage
questions.C: kill all the pests living in the soil
questions.D: increase the rate of erosion on the farm
questions.explanation: Yam and cassava are commonly grown on ridges or mounds.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Minimum (zero) tillage is recommended because it
questions.A: increases the labour needed on the farm
questions.B: destroys the structure of the soil
questions.C: conserves soil moisture, reduces erosion and saves cost
questions.explanation: Crop residues are left on the surface and seeds are planted directly with little disturbance.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The removal of tree stumps and roots after clearing is called
questions.explanation: Stumping allows machinery to work without obstruction.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a disadvantage of bush burning during land preparation?
questions.A: it destroys humus and soil organisms and exposes the soil
questions.B: it clears the land quickly and cheaply
questions.C: it kills some of the pests in the bush
questions.D: it releases some nutrients in the ash
questions.explanation: The short-term ash benefit is outweighed by the loss of humus, nitrogen and micro-organisms.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A fine, crumbly seedbed prepared for planting small seeds is described as having a good
questions.explanation: Tilth is the physical condition of the soil after tillage.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Deep ploughing of a sandy soil in the savanna during the dry season is undesirable because it
questions.A: increases the yield of the next crop
questions.B: increases the organic matter in the soil
questions.D: exposes the soil to wind erosion and moisture loss
questions.explanation: Tillage should be timed with the rains and kept shallow on light soils.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following mechanised implements is used for primary tillage?
questions.explanation: Disc and mouldboard ploughs perform primary tillage.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Heaps or mounds are commonly made for planting
questions.explanation: Mounds give the deep loose soil needed for large yam tubers.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The part of the plant that anchors it in the soil and absorbs water and mineral salts is the
questions.explanation: Root hairs increase the surface area for absorption; roots may also store food, as in cassava.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Plants that complete their life cycle in one growing season are called
questions.explanation: Maize, rice and cowpea are annuals; cocoa and oil palm are perennials.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The process by which green plants manufacture food using sunlight, carbon dioxide and water is
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll traps light energy to make glucose and release oxygen.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The loss of water vapour from the leaves of a plant through the stomata is called
questions.explanation: Transpiration cools the plant and pulls water and minerals up from the roots.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A plant with a fibrous root system, parallel-veined leaves and seeds with one cotyledon is a
questions.explanation: Maize, rice and sorghum are monocots; cowpea, groundnut and cocoa are dicots with tap roots.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The tissue that transports water and dissolved minerals from the roots to the leaves is the
questions.explanation: Xylem carries water upward; phloem translocates manufactured food.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Germination in which the cotyledons are carried above the soil surface is called
questions.explanation: Cowpea and groundnut show epigeal germination; maize shows hypogeal germination.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following conditions is necessary for seed germination?
questions.explanation: Water activates enzymes, oxygen allows respiration and warmth speeds the process; viability is also needed.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The failure of a viable seed to germinate even under favourable conditions is called
questions.explanation: Dormancy may be broken by scarification, soaking, heat or chilling.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Growth in plants is best described as
questions.A: a temporary increase in the size of the plant
questions.B: the loss of leaves during the dry season
questions.C: a permanent increase in size and dry weight
questions.D: the movement of the shoot towards light
questions.explanation: Growth involves cell division, enlargement and differentiation.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The growth movement of a plant shoot towards light is called
questions.explanation: Roots show positive geotropism and shoots positive phototropism.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The plant hormone responsible for cell elongation and apical dominance is
questions.explanation: Auxins are used commercially in rooting powders and as selective herbicides (2,4-D).

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a modified stem used for food storage?
questions.explanation: Yam and Irish potato tubers are stem tubers; cassava, carrot and sweet potato are root tubers.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The female reproductive part of a flower consists of the
questions.explanation: The pistil (carpel) receives pollen on the stigma; the ovary contains ovules that become seeds.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Pollen grains are produced in the
questions.explanation: The stamen (male part) consists of the anther and filament.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Maize is described as monoecious because
questions.A: it bears separate male and female flowers on the same plant
questions.B: male and female flowers are borne on separate plants
questions.C: its flowers contain both male and female parts
questions.D: it does not produce any flowers at all
questions.explanation: Pawpaw is dioecious (male and female plants separate); cowpea has bisexual (hermaphrodite) flowers.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The stomata of a leaf are guarded by
questions.explanation: Guard cells open and close the stomatal pores to control gas exchange and water loss.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Dry weight of a plant is used to measure growth because it
questions.C: is easier to measure than height
questions.explanation: Fresh weight fluctuates with water uptake; dry matter reflects true accumulation of material.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Cassava is propagated by
questions.explanation: Mature stem cuttings 20–30 cm long with several nodes are planted upright or slanting.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Plantain and banana are propagated mainly by
questions.explanation: Sword suckers with narrow leaves are preferred; the tissue-culture method is also used.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma of the same flower or plant is
questions.explanation: Cowpea and rice are largely self-pollinated; maize and oil palm are cross-pollinated.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is an agent of cross-pollination?
questions.explanation: Wind pollinates grasses such as maize; bees pollinate many fruits and vegetables.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Fertilisation in flowering plants is the
questions.A: transfer of pollen from anther to stigma
questions.B: shedding of pollen grains by the anther
questions.C: opening of the flower bud in the morning
questions.D: fusion of the male gamete with the egg cell in the ovule
questions.explanation: After fertilisation the ovule becomes the seed and the ovary becomes the fruit.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The method of vegetative propagation in which a bud from a desirable plant is inserted under the bark of a rootstock is
questions.explanation: Budding is widely used for citrus, rubber and roses.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: In grafting, the upper part that provides the desired fruiting variety is the
questions.explanation: The scion is joined to a rootstock chosen for vigour or disease resistance.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Marcotting (air layering) involves
questions.A: planting seeds in a nursery bed for later transplanting
questions.B: joining the stem of one plant to the root of another
questions.C: cutting stems into short pieces for planting
questions.D: rooting a branch while it is still attached to the parent plant
questions.explanation: A ring of bark is removed, the wound is wrapped in moist soil and polythene, and the rooted branch is later cut off.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: An advantage of vegetative propagation over seed propagation is that
questions.A: it produces plenty of variation among the offspring
questions.B: offspring are identical to the parent and mature earlier
questions.C: it spreads viral diseases less than seeds do
questions.D: it can be used for every crop that is grown
questions.explanation: Clones keep desirable characters but also transmit viruses if the parent is infected.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Yam is propagated by
questions.explanation: Whole small tubers (seed yams) or cut pieces (setts) with skin are planted in mounds.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following crops is normally raised in a nursery before transplanting?
questions.explanation: Tomato, pepper, cocoa, oil palm and rice (in some systems) are raised in nurseries.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Seeds that are covered with a hard coat may be made to germinate quickly by
questions.B: freezing them in a refrigerator overnight
questions.C: planting them deeper in the soil
questions.D: drying them in the sun for a month
questions.explanation: Scarification or soaking in hot water helps water enter the seed.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A cocoa farmer wants all his new trees to have exactly the high yield and pod characteristics of one outstanding tree. The best propagation method is
questions.A: budding or cuttings taken from the tree
questions.B: planting seeds collected from the tree
questions.C: planting seeds bought from the market
questions.D: sowing seeds of a different variety
questions.explanation: Seeds from cross-pollinated cocoa vary; vegetative propagation gives identical clones.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Sugar cane and pineapple are propagated by
questions.explanation: Sugar cane setts with two or three buds are planted in furrows; pineapple uses suckers, slips and crowns.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The advantage of seed propagation includes
questions.A: offspring identical to the parent plant
questions.B: absence of dormancy in the seeds
questions.C: early maturity of the new plants
questions.D: ease of storage and creation of new varieties
questions.explanation: Seeds are cheap, easy to handle and allow breeders to select from the variation they produce.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Growing the same crop on the same piece of land year after year is called
questions.explanation: Monocropping exhausts specific nutrients and builds up pests and diseases.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Planting a second crop into a standing crop before the first is harvested is called
questions.explanation: Relay cropping, e.g. cassava planted into maturing maize, makes fuller use of the season.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: In a four-year rotation, a leguminous crop such as cowpea is included in order to
questions.explanation: Legumes also provide a break in the cycle of cereal pests and diseases.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: In crop rotation, a deep-rooted crop should follow a shallow-rooted crop in order to
questions.A: use nutrients from different soil depths
questions.B: increase the rate of erosion on the farm
questions.C: reduce the yield of the following crop
questions.D: shade the soil from the sun completely
questions.explanation: Alternating rooting depths and nutrient demands keeps the whole profile productive.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Growing crops in alternate strips across a slope with a cover crop is called
questions.explanation: Strip cropping controls erosion on sloping land.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The number of plants per unit area of land is called
questions.explanation: Plant density is calculated from the spacing: area ÷ (row spacing × within-row spacing).

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: At a spacing of 1 m × 1 m, the plant population per hectare (one plant per stand) is

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The plant population per hectare of cassava planted at 1 m × 0.8 m is

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Ley farming refers to
questions.A: the growing of tree crops only on an estate
questions.B: planting crops on steep hill slopes
questions.C: fish farming in flooded rice fields
questions.D: alternating arable crops with sown pasture for grazing
questions.explanation: The grass/legume ley restores fertility and structure while feeding livestock.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of intercropping?
questions.A: it makes the use of farm machinery easier
questions.B: it insures against total crop failure and uses land fully
questions.C: it increases the build-up of pests of one crop
questions.D: it simplifies the harvesting of the crops
questions.explanation: Mixtures of crops with different heights, rooting depths and maturity periods share resources efficiently.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Alley cropping is the growing of arable crops
questions.A: in the shade of a natural forest
questions.D: on ridges only during the rains
questions.explanation: Leucaena and Gliricidia hedgerows supply nitrogen-rich mulch and fuelwood.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Taungya farming is a system in which
questions.A: food crops are grown among young forest trees
questions.B: fish are raised in flooded rice fields
questions.C: cattle graze under fruit trees in orchards
questions.D: crops are grown under glass in greenhouses
questions.explanation: The forestry department gets its plantation established cheaply while the farmer gets land for a few years.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A farmer plants 10,000 maize stands per hectare with two seeds per hole. If the seed rate is 25 kg/ha, the average weight of one maize seed is
questions.explanation: Seeds used = 20,000; 25,000 g ÷ 20,000 = 1.25 g per seed.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Mixed farming is a system in which
questions.A: crops and livestock are produced on the same farm
questions.B: several crops are grown together on one field
questions.C: farmers move from one place to another
questions.D: only vegetables are grown near the towns
questions.explanation: Livestock supply manure and draught power, and crop residues feed the animals.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following planting patterns is used for tree crops such as cocoa and oil palm?
questions.C: square or triangular planting at set spacing
questions.explanation: Oil palm is planted in a triangular pattern at about 9 m spacing (143 palms per hectare).

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Maize belongs to the family
questions.explanation: Grasses include maize, rice, sorghum, millet, wheat and sugar cane.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Cowpea, groundnut and soya bean belong to the family
questions.explanation: Legumes bear pods and fix nitrogen in root nodules.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Tomato, pepper and Irish potato belong to the family
questions.explanation: Members of the Solanaceae share pests such as the fruit worm and diseases such as blight.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The optimum planting depth for maize seed is about
questions.explanation: Shallow planting risks drying and bird damage; deep planting exhausts the seed reserves before emergence.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Rice grown in flooded fields is called
questions.explanation: Swamp rice gives higher yields than upland rice and is grown in fadama and irrigated schemes.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Yam is harvested about
questions.explanation: Early harvesting (milking) may be done at 5–6 months for some varieties, followed by a second harvest.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Cocoa seedlings are usually transplanted at the age of
questions.explanation: Seedlings are raised in polythene bags in a shaded nursery and transplanted at the start of the rains.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Oil palm starts to bear fruit about
questions.explanation: Tenera hybrids from NIFOR come into bearing in 3–4 years and peak at 8–15 years.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The removal of unwanted branches or shoots from crops such as cocoa and citrus is called
questions.explanation: Pruning shapes the tree, removes diseased wood and improves air circulation and fruiting.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Thinning is carried out in a crop stand in order to
questions.B: remove excess seedlings and give the rest space
questions.C: add more plants to the stand
questions.D: kill the weeds among the crop
questions.explanation: Where several seeds were sown per hole, seedlings are thinned to the desired number.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Supplying is the practice of
questions.A: applying fertiliser to the young crop
questions.explanation: Supplying is done within one to two weeks of planting so that the new plants catch up.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Earthing up (moulding) is carried out in crops such as Irish potato and groundnut in order to
questions.A: expose the developing tubers to light
questions.B: cover the tubers or pegs with soil and support the plants
questions.C: reduce the number of plants in the field
questions.D: attract pollinating insects to the flowers
questions.explanation: Exposed potato tubers turn green and poisonous; groundnut pegs need loose soil to enter.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Cotton is grown mainly for its
questions.explanation: Lint goes to textile mills; cottonseed yields oil and cake.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Groundnut is harvested when
questions.A: the first flowers open on the plants
questions.B: the leaves yellow and the inner pod shell darkens
questions.C: the plants are two weeks old
questions.D: the pods are still green and soft
questions.explanation: Delayed harvesting leads to pods being left in the soil and aflatoxin contamination.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Kola nut and cocoa are classified as
questions.explanation: Beverage crops include cocoa, coffee, tea and kola.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is an oil crop?
questions.explanation: Oil crops include groundnut, oil palm, soya bean, coconut, sesame and melon.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A farmer's maize crop lodged (fell over) badly after a storm. The most likely agronomic causes are
questions.B: excess nitrogen, low potassium and stem-borer damage
questions.D: the use of certified hybrid seed
questions.explanation: Weak stalks from unbalanced nutrition and borer tunnels make plants prone to lodging.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The recommended spacing for maize in Nigeria is about
questions.explanation: 75 cm between rows and 25 cm within rows gives about 53,000 plants per hectare.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The staking of yam vines is done in order to
questions.B: expose the leaves to sunlight and reduce disease
questions.C: prevent birds from eating the leaves
questions.D: reduce the size of the tubers
questions.explanation: Staked yams give higher yields than unstaked ones.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following crops is a cereal?
questions.explanation: Cereals are grasses grown for their grain: maize, rice, sorghum, millet, wheat.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Harvesting of cassava is best done
questions.B: between 9 and 18 months, depending on variety
questions.D: when the leaves are wet with dew
questions.explanation: Delayed harvesting beyond 18 months makes the roots woody.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: An area of land covered with grasses and legumes on which animals graze is called
questions.explanation: Pastures may be natural (rangeland) or established (sown).

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a pasture grass?
questions.explanation: Guinea grass, elephant grass, Gamba grass and giant star grass are pasture grasses; the others are legumes.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a pasture legume?
questions.explanation: Centrosema, Stylosanthes, Calopogonium and Pueraria improve pasture protein and fix nitrogen.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The system of grazing in which the pasture is divided into paddocks that are grazed in turn is
questions.explanation: Rotational grazing allows pasture recovery, reduces parasite build-up and prevents overgrazing.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Zero grazing means that
questions.A: animals graze freely in the field all day
questions.B: animals are kept in stalls and fodder is carried to them
questions.C: no animals of any kind are kept
questions.D: the pasture is burnt before grazing
questions.explanation: Cut-and-carry feeding is used for dairy cows and in areas of land shortage.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Green fodder preserved by fermentation in a silo is called
questions.explanation: Silage is made from chopped maize, sorghum or elephant grass stored without air.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Hay is
questions.B: grass or legume cut and dried for storage
questions.C: chopped grass fermented in a silo
questions.explanation: Hay is made in dry weather; over-drying loses leaves and nutrients.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Overgrazing of pasture results in
questions.B: bare soil, erosion and invasion by unpalatable weeds
questions.C: higher milk yield from the cows
questions.explanation: Stocking rate must match the carrying capacity of the pasture.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The cultivation of flowers and ornamental plants is called
questions.explanation: Floriculture supplies cut flowers, potted plants and landscape plants and is a growing urban business.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is an ornamental plant?
questions.explanation: Hibiscus, bougainvillea, ixora, croton and roses are common ornamentals in Nigeria.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Ornamental plants are important because they
questions.A: provide the staple food of the people
questions.B: beautify the environment and provide shade and income
questions.C: are used as the main feed for cattle
questions.explanation: Landscaping of homes, offices and roads uses trees, shrubs, hedges and lawns.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A pasture is said to have reached its carrying capacity when
questions.A: it can support no more animals without damage
questions.B: all the grass on it has been eaten
questions.C: the grass on it is at its tallest
questions.D: it has just been sown with grass seed
questions.explanation: Carrying capacity is the maximum number of animals a pasture can support over a period without damage.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Lawns are usually established with
questions.explanation: Low-growing, creeping grasses tolerate mowing and trampling.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following factors affects the productivity of a pasture?
questions.A: the colour of the animals grazing it
questions.B: soil fertility, rainfall and grazing management
questions.C: the age of the farmer who owns it
questions.D: the shape of the paddock gate
questions.explanation: Fertilisation, controlled stocking and legume inclusion increase pasture yield.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A weed is best defined as
questions.B: a plant growing where it is not wanted
questions.D: a poisonous plant in the field
questions.explanation: A maize plant in a cassava field is a weed; weeds compete with crops for water, light, nutrients and space.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a parasitic weed of sorghum, millet and maize in the savanna?
questions.explanation: Striga attaches to the host's roots and can cause total crop loss on poor soils.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Spear grass (Imperata cylindrica) is difficult to control because it
questions.A: has no roots in the soil
questions.D: dies as soon as it is cut once
questions.explanation: Repeated deep hoeing, shading with cover crops and systemic herbicides such as glyphosate are used.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Weeds reduce crop yield mainly by
questions.A: adding too much nitrogen to the soil
questions.B: competing with crops for nutrients, water and light
questions.C: attracting heavy rain to the farm
questions.D: improving the structure of the soil
questions.explanation: Weeds also harbour pests and diseases and contaminate harvested produce.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The removal of weeds with hoes and cutlasses is called
questions.explanation: Hand weeding is effective but laborious and slow.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A herbicide that kills weeds before the crop emerges from the soil is described as
questions.explanation: Pre-emergence herbicides such as atrazine are applied to the soil soon after planting.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A selective herbicide is one that
questions.A: kills every plant in the field
questions.B: kills certain weeds without harming the crop
questions.explanation: 2,4-D kills broad-leaved weeds in cereals without damaging the grass crop.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The use of natural enemies such as insects to control weeds like water hyacinth is
questions.explanation: Weevils have been released against water hyacinth on Nigerian waterways.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a cultural method of weed control?
questions.explanation: Cultural methods use farm practices to suppress weeds.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Weeds that complete their life cycle within one year are called
questions.explanation: Annual weeds such as Tridax and goat weed are controlled by preventing seeding.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A farmer who applies a non-selective systemic herbicide to a field of young maize would most likely
questions.B: kill both the weeds and the maize
questions.explanation: Non-selective herbicides such as glyphosate kill all green plants they contact and are translocated throughout the plant.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Some weeds are beneficial because they
questions.B: serve as cover crops, fodder and green manure
questions.D: reduce the fertility of the soil
questions.explanation: Leguminous weeds add nitrogen; grasses protect the soil and feed livestock.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following weeds is dispersed by wind?
questions.explanation: Tridax has hairy fruits (pappus) carried by wind; Imperata spreads mainly by rhizomes.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Nut grass (Cyperus rotundus) is a difficult weed because it reproduces through
questions.explanation: Each fragment of tuber can produce a new plant.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A plant disease is caused by
questions.A: excess sunshine on the leaves only
questions.B: pathogens such as fungi, bacteria and viruses
questions.C: hoes and cutlasses used on the farm
questions.explanation: Diseases may also be physiological (nutrient deficiency), but infectious diseases are caused by pathogens.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Cassava mosaic disease is caused by
questions.explanation: Symptoms are mottled, distorted leaves; control is by resistant varieties and clean cuttings.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Black pod disease of cocoa is caused by
questions.D: an insect that bores the pod
questions.explanation: Black pod thrives in wet weather; it is controlled by copper fungicides, pruning and removal of infected pods.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Cocoa swollen shoot disease is caused by a
questions.explanation: Infected trees are cut out and destroyed; there is no chemical cure for viral diseases.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Maize smut is caused by
questions.explanation: Smut produces black powdery galls on the ear; rust and blight are other fungal diseases of maize.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Groundnut rosette disease is transmitted by
questions.explanation: Rosette virus causes stunting and yellow, bunched leaves; early planting and close spacing reduce it.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a bacterial disease of crops?
questions.explanation: Bacterial blight causes angular leaf spots, wilting and die-back.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Root-knot of tomato and okra is caused by
questions.explanation: Root-knot nematodes produce galls on roots; control by rotation, resistant varieties and nematicides.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Damping-off of seedlings in the nursery is caused by
questions.explanation: Over-watering, dense sowing and poor drainage favour damping-off; sterilised soil and fungicides control it.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The systematic destruction of diseased plants to prevent spread is called
questions.explanation: Roguing is essential in seed production fields and against viral diseases.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a method of controlling fungal diseases?
questions.A: application of insecticide to the leaves
questions.B: spraying fungicides and using resistant varieties
questions.C: irrigation of the field in the evening
questions.D: application of urea to the soil
questions.explanation: Cultural methods (rotation, sanitation) and chemical fungicides are combined.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Viral diseases of crops are best controlled by
questions.A: spraying copper fungicides on the leaves each week
questions.B: controlling vectors and using clean planting material
questions.C: applying nematicides to the soil before planting
questions.D: watering the plants every morning and evening
questions.explanation: Once a plant is infected with a virus it cannot be cured.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A tomato farmer notices wilting plants with brown rings inside the cut stems, and a milky ooze from the cut end when placed in water. The likely disease is
questions.explanation: The bacterial streaming test is diagnostic of bacterial wilt (Ralstonia); control by rotation and resistant varieties.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Yam tuber rot in storage is caused mainly by
questions.explanation: Careful handling, curing and storage in well-ventilated barns reduce rot.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The mosaic pattern on infected leaves refers to
questions.A: holes eaten in the leaves by insects
questions.B: patches of light and dark green caused by viruses
questions.D: white powder on the leaf surface
questions.explanation: Mosaic symptoms are typical of viral infections such as cassava mosaic and tobacco mosaic.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: An insect pest that bites and chews plant parts has
questions.explanation: Grasshoppers, caterpillars, beetles and termites chew; aphids, mealybugs and capsids pierce and suck.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Insects such as aphids and cotton stainers damage crops by
questions.explanation: Sucking insects cause curling and yellowing of leaves and spread viral diseases.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The stem borer is a major pest of
questions.explanation: Larvae tunnel in the stem, causing dead hearts and lodging; control by early planting, destruction of residues and insecticides.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Capsids (mirids) are important pests of
questions.explanation: Capsids pierce pods and shoots, causing die-back; controlled with insecticides and good canopy management.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The pest that attacks stored cowpea seeds, boring circular holes in them, is
questions.explanation: Callosobruchus maculatus is controlled by storing dry seeds in airtight containers or with ash, oil or fumigants.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The maize weevil damages stored maize by
questions.B: boring into the grains and feeding inside
questions.explanation: Sitophilus zeamais reduces grain weight and quality; dry grain to below 13% moisture and fumigate stores.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a non-insect pest of crops?
questions.explanation: Rodents, birds, monkeys, nematodes, snails and millipedes are non-insect pests.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The stage of the butterfly or moth that causes most damage to crops is the
questions.explanation: Caterpillars chew leaves, bore stems and fruits; army worms can strip a whole field.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
